lessonRef.subject: mathematics
lessonRef.unitTitle: Quantitative Reasoning, Units, and Rational Exponents
lessonRef.focus: quantities, units, and derived rates in context
lessonRef.title: Investigation or close reading: quantities, units, and derived rates in context

sections.title: Instructional examples
sections.directions: This example shows the kind of reasoning the investigation asks for.

steps: Subtracting the rational number 5 would leave √3 rational, but √3 is irrational.
The assumption fails, so 5 + √3 is irrational.

sections.title: Guided practice
sections.directions: Talk through what changes and what stays fixed before you answer.

items.prompt: Option A delivers 33 units of output over 3 hours. Option B delivers 32 units over 4 hours. Which has the greater output per hour?
choices: There is not enough information without knowing the total hours available.

items.prompt: A rectangular plot measures 85.3 m by 10.8 m, each measured to the nearest tenth of a metre. Report the area to 2 decimal places.

sections.title: Independent practice
sections.directions: Work on your own. Show the steps that produced each answer.

items.prompt: You are building a model of the rate at which a reservoir is draining. Which unit should the modelled quantity be reported in?
A delivery drone operates at 73 kilometers per hour. Express this rate in meters per minute.
Rewrite the index-4 radical expression 4√(x^3) using a rational exponent, in lowest terms.

sections.title: Extension and challenge
sections.directions: Write out the reasoning in full sentences. A correct answer with no justification does not count here.

items.responseExpectation: Give the result and the reasoning that produced it. Show enough work that someone else could check each step.

items.prompt: Classify the sum of the rational number 3 and the irrational number √10 as rational or irrational, and be ready to justify it.
items.responseExpectation: Give the result and the reasoning that produced it. Show enough work that someone else could check each step.
